author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory filtered by specialty (browser page)
summary: The browser veterinarian directory can be narrowed to veterinarians holding a named specialty via the request address; the filtered list stays paged and its page-to-page links carry the chosen specialty.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the browser page is opened for that specialty, then only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time.
Given a filtered result spanning more than one page, when a page-to-page link is followed, then the chosen specialty still applies to the page reached.
Given a specialty differing from a stored specialty name only by letter case, the page matches; a value matching only the start of a specialty name matches nothing (whole-name, case-insensitive).
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the browser page is opened, then the page is shown with an empty veterinarian list and a success response rather than an error.
Given a blank, whitespace-only, or absent specialty, when the browser page is opened, then the full directory is listed exactly as before the filter existed.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search (NG-9 keeps this out)
Any page control — form, dropdown, or link — for the filter in this round
notes: Narrows NG-9 (see adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md). Open question, taken at the narrowest reading pending confirmation: only a wholly empty/whitespace value is treated as absent (owner-search parity); whether surrounding whitespace on a NON-empty specialty value is trimmed before the whole-name match is unspecified — narrowest reading matches the value as given. Resurface via consultation if implementation needs it.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Machine-readable veterinarian list reinstated and filtered by specialty
summary: The machine-readable veterinarian list is a supported surface again; its first requested capability is a specialty filter that returns only the veterinarians holding the named specialty. The withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id is not reused.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable list is requested for that specialty, then only those veterinarians are returned.
Given a specialty differing from a stored specialty name only by letter case, the list matches; a value matching only the start of a specialty name matches nothing (whole-name, case-insensitive).
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the machine-readable list is requested, then an empty veterinarian list is returned with a success response rather than an error.
Given a blank, whitespace-only, or absent specialty, when the machine-readable list is requested, then every veterinarian is returned (today's unfiltered behavior).
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search (NG-9 keeps this out)
Pagination of the machine-readable list — it stays unpaginated as today, returning the whole matching set
notes: Reinstates the /vets surface withdrawn as REQ-VET-002 (Superseded); the id is not reused. Depends on REQ-VET-003 for the shared repository-level specialty filter. Narrowest-reading open question on non-empty-whitespace trimming carries over from the REQ-VET-003 record.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the established Spring Data derived-query + paginated-controller pattern (system-design.md Contracts: VetController/VetRepository) to a new field. The shared repository-level filter is a new derived query on VetRepository matching the held specialty by whole name, case-insensitively; VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty param and routes to the filtered or unfiltered paged query. Mirrors OwnerController.processFindForm / OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith (Read-confirmed; IDE oracle not available this run) but with whole-name EQUALITY, not prefix StartingWith. No new module, no new pattern, no ADR needed — the product decision is already recorded in adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md. system-design.md updated: VetController/VetRepository Implements rewired to add REQ-VET-003/004.
integration_points: New VetRepository derived query: Page<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) traverses Vet.specialties -> Specialty.name; the IgnoreCase keyword compiles to upper(s.name)=upper(?), giving whole-name case-insensitive match in the query itself

VetController.showVetList gains @RequestParam(required=false) String specialty; branches: blank/whitespace/absent -> existing findAll(pageable); non-blank -> the filtered paged query. totalPages/currentPage flow unchanged from the filtered Page
vetList.html page links must carry the specialty param (currently @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} drops it); controller adds specialty to the model so every page-to-page link re-applies the filter

patterns.description: paginated repository-filter derived query — the shape to mirror, but whole-name equality (IgnoreCase) not prefix (StartingWith)
existing addPaginationModel/findPaginated pagination helper the filtered path reuses

risks.risk: Blank/whitespace/absent specialty must return the FULL list. OwnerController collapses a blank last name to "" because StartingWith("") matches all — but whole-name equality on "" matches NOTHING, so copying that trick would wrongly empty the list.
risks.mitigation: Controller branches on isBlank(): blank -> existing findAll(pageable) unfiltered path; only a non-blank value reaches the filter query. Do not feed "" into the specialty query.

risks.risk: Case-insensitivity must not lean on column collation — the PostgreSQL owner-search case-sensitivity Known Defect (REQ-OWN-002) came from exactly that.
risks.mitigation: Use the Spring Data IgnoreCase derived-query keyword (or explicit upper()=upper() JPQL) so the match is vendor-neutral in the query, not the schema.

risks.risk: New filter methods sharing @Cacheable("vets") with the existing findAll methods; the vet cache has no eviction (Open Question 5).
risks.mitigation: SimpleKeyGenerator keys differ by arity/type from the existing findAll()/findAll(Pageable) keys, so no collision. Vet/specialty data is static seed data, so per-specialty cache growth is bounded and consistent with the existing pattern — mirror the annotation, or leave the filter methods uncached; either is acceptable, but keep it a deliberate choice.

risks.risk: ManyToMany specialties is EAGER; a paged query with a collection join can trigger HHH000104 in-memory pagination or duplicate root rows.
risks.mitigation: The filter join is a WHERE predicate, not a fetch join, so pagination stays on the Vet root; a vet holds a given specialty at most once, so no duplicates. Verify no HHH000104 warning in the test run; add DISTINCT only if duplicates actually appear.

notes: Whitespace open question (carried from the prd-entry): narrowest reading is to detect blank via isBlank() but match a NON-empty value as-given (no .strip()), unlike OwnerController which strips. If the implementer wants trim-before-match parity with owner search, that is a behavioral change — resurface via consultation rather than deciding it silently. REQ-VET-004 is triaged in a sibling design-block sharing this analysis; its JSON surface consumes the same repository filter.

No pagination on this surface (non-goal): the whole matching set is returned

patterns.description: existing @ResponseBody Vets-wrapper route the filter parameterizes

risks.risk: Same blank-vs-empty inversion as REQ-VET-003: a blank/absent specialty must return ALL vets, not an empty set.
risks.mitigation: Branch on isBlank() to the unfiltered findAll(); only a non-blank value reaches the filter query.

notes: The withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id is NOT reused (see adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md and prd Superseded). Whitespace open question carries over identically from REQ-VET-003: match a non-empty value as-given under the narrowest reading; consult before adding trim-before-match. This record shares the full pattern/guardrail analysis in the REQ-VET-003 design-block (handoff line 5).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Specialty filter uses Spring Data derived query (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) with bound parameters — no JPQL/SQL string concatenation, not injectable
Reflected specialty value reaches only Thymeleaf @{...} URL expressions, which URL-encode query-parameter values; no th:utext or unescaped attribute sink, so no reflected XSS
Pagination links target the fixed /vets.html path with specialty as a query-param value only — no host/path/protocol control, so no open redirect
Both controller methods branch null/blank specialty to unfiltered findAll; only non-blank values reach the bound query — no trust-boundary bypass
JSON /vets route reuses the same bound query and relies on Jackson output escaping

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Both filter methods carry @Cacheable("vets") with no explanation. The design-block records the reasoning (SimpleKeyGenerator keys differ by arity so no collision with findAll variants; vet/specialty data is static seed data so cache growth is bounded), but none of that reaches the code. A reader who later adds dynamic specialty management will not know whether the shared-cache annotation was a deliberate, reasoned choice or an accidental copy. A brief inline why-comment on each filter method restores the intent.
findings.fix: Add a comment above each @Cacheable("vets") on the filter overloads, e.g.: // Shares the 'vets' cache deliberately: SimpleKeyGenerator keys differ by arity from findAll variants (no collision); specialty data is static seed data so per-key growth is bounded.

findings.description: addPaginationModel stores the raw specialty value in the model regardless of whether it is null or blank. Null is correct (Thymeleaf omits it from pagination URLs), but a blank value (e.g., specialty=   from a browser) propagates as-is and produces specialty=%20%20%20 in every pagination link. The controller already treats blank as unfiltered in findPaginated; the model should reflect the same normalisation so pagination URLs are clean.
findings.fix: Before model.addAttribute("specialty", specialty), normalise: String specialtyForModel = (specialty == null || specialty.isBlank()) ? null : specialty; model.addAttribute("specialty", specialtyForModel);

approved_aspects: Blank-vs-null branch (isBlank() guard) correctly prevents empty-string from reaching the filter query
findPaginated private helper cleanly centralises the paged filter logic with single responsibility
showResourcesVetList branch mirrors findPaginated intent consistently for the unpaged surface
vetList.html Thymeleaf param syntax correctly carries specialty through all five pagination link sites
@Cacheable SimpleKeyGenerator key analysis is sound: filter keys are distinct from findAll keys so no cache collision
IgnoreCase derived-query keyword gives vendor-neutral case-insensitive match without collation dependency
DataAccessException declared on new methods consistent with pre-existing interface style
Javadoc on both new repository methods is specific and accurate
